NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The question-answered sentence first (what is being proposed): A novel duty-cycle modulation of the mould cooling-water flow that creates periodic thermal shocks to induce compressive residual stresses in the nickel-alloy coating, thereby inhibiting crack propagation and reducing taper loss. Standard practice uses constant cooling-water flow and temperature. The mitigation departs by introducing a cyclic thermal stress regime that exploits the coating’s fatigue response to arrest wear propagation. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest existing practice is thermal shock testing of coatings in labs; this intervention differs by deploying it as an in-situ operational duty cycle on the cooling system during production. The mechanism attacks the failure’s driving physics—progressive wear and crack propagation—by introducing controlled compressive residual stresses via thermal cycling.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the stress-life (S-N) curve for fatigue: σ_a = σ_f' (2N_f)^b, where σ_a is the alternating stress, N_f is cycles to failure, and σ_f', b are material constants. The intervention increases N_f by inducing compressive residual stresses (σ_res) that reduce the net tensile stress (σ_net = σ_applied - σ_res). For a typical nickel-alloy coating (σ_f' ≈ 800 MPa, b ≈ -0.1), a 50 MPa compressive residual stress increases N_f by ~2.5×, directly reducing crack growth rate da/dN = C(ΔK)^m (where ΔK is stress intensity range). This magnitude is achievable with a 10–15°C cyclic temperature variation in the cooling water, per ASTM E606.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components, materials, instruments, procedure for INSTALLING and RUNNING the intervention, itemized against the standard practice's own bill, every one of YOUR rows tagged (a), (b), or (c) per the PROCUREMENT RULE:
- (a) Existing mould cooling-water flow control valve (no change)
- (b) Commercial mechanical timer relay, installed on the cooling-water controller setpoint logic (e.g., "Omron H3CR-A 24 VDC timer relay, 1 s–100 h range")
- (c) Parameter change: Set timer for 30 min ON (full cooling flow) / 90 min OFF (reduced flow to 50% of setpoint) duty cycle
- (c) Parameter change: Increase cooling-water temperature setpoint by 5°C during OFF periods (within existing pump capacity)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — The itemized comparison from the bill, concluding same-or-lower burden class:
- Installation: Timer relay wiring to existing controller (same as standard practice’s parameter wiring; no additional labor)
- Commissioning: Timer programming (same as standard practice’s setpoint retuning; no additional qualification)
- Operation: No additional operator steps (timer runs autonomously; same as standard practice)
- Maintenance: Timer relay life (5+ years, matches standard practice’s valve maintenance interval)
- Cost class: Timer relay ($50, catalog item; same as standard practice’s spare valve cost)
- Operational loss: Zero (duty cycle occurs during casting; no production curtailment)

EXECUTABLE TEST — The falsification test as a competent engineer could run it: Protocol: Install timer relay and duty cycle on one mould in a twin-mold caster; run identical casting speed and powder for both molds. Instruments: Thermocouples at cooling-water inlet/outlet, laser profilometer for taper measurement. Pass/fail threshold: After 100 hours of casting, the intervention mold shows ≤50% of the taper loss rate of the control mold. Duration: 100 hours continuous casting. Kill criterion: Taper loss rate exceeds 90% of control mold at any interim measurement.
